title: Bai Garden Grafting Chronicle
premise: A long grafting drama of the nursery and rootstock beds. Aya and Asui look nearly alike and are easily mistaken; the grafting knife goes sharp→chipped→rehoned; the orchard tractor is wrecked and must be avoided; scion bundles / bamboo tags / wind chimes count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Fruit-tree grafting master Qiao Bai around fifty, straw hat and green rubber boots, grafting-knife sheath at the waist, resin stains on both hands.
states.weary_wounded: The same Qiao Bai: rubber boots cracked, knee bandaged, walking slowly with a peach-wood cane, straw hat still on.
states.stepped_away: Qiao Bai has left the post; only his green rubber boots and straw hat remain in the nursery—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Apprentice Aya of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf and yellow vest, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Aya in the twenties, still the indigo headscarf, upright and steady.

states.blade_sharp: A short-handled grafting knife, blade like a mirror, wood handle carved Bai, cowhide sheath.
states.blade_chipped: The same grafting knife with a chipped blade, rough cut edge, wood handle thick with resin.
states.rehoned: After rehoning the grafting knife blade is sharp again; the Bai on the handle remains, fine grind marks left.

states.intact: An oilcloth-cover phenology notebook logging budbreak, bloom, and graft survival rates.
states.mud_stained: The same phenology notebook soaked through by muddy water, cover wrinkled, writing bled.

states.intact: A red orchard tractor with rootstock seedlings in the bed, white Bai Garden letters sprayed on the door.
states.rollover_wrecked: After rolling on a slope, the orchard tractor has a twisted bed and broken front wheel—a wreck.

states.young_rival: Young Asui whose face closely resembles Aya's, cream silk scarf and the same yellow vest, flamboyant look.
states.remade_face: After remaking the look, Asui still wears the cream silk scarf, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk, Qiao Bai enters the nursery shed and first wipes the grafting knife at his waist.
A row of five bamboo tags sticks in the rootstock berm; Qiao Bai checks each handwritten date.
Two wind chimes hang under the shed eaves; Qiao Bai reaches to make them chime softly.
Qiao Bai circles the workbench checking whether the wax seals have set.
From the shed Qiao Bai looks toward the darkening green seedlings of the rootstock bed.
The grafting-knife blade mirrors lamp light; Qiao Bai gently tests the edge.
Qiao Bai sits on a bamboo chair in the shed corner for a brief rest.
Qiao Bai opens the phenology notebook—this oilcloth phenology book—and marks plump bud-eye spots bed by bed.
Qiao Bai draws rootstock budbreak progress in green line and marks bud-graft survival with red dots.
Qiao Bai closes the phenology book and returns it to the workbench wood box of wax seals and ties.
The grafting knife clicks into its sheath; Qiao Bai nods.
Qiao Bai wipes mud flecks from the cover with a dry cloth and tucks in a budded scion as a specimen.
At the morning rootstock bed, Qiao Bai greets young Aya arriving in the orchard tractor.
Aya jumps down from the tractor and rights the rootstock seedlings in the bed.
Qiao Bai points to the three Fuji scion bundles in the shed shade and teaches Aya to read plump bud eyes.
Aya crouches on the berm, curiously touching the writing on the bamboo tags.
Qiao Bai explains bud-graft angle; Aya nods carefully.
Aya glances back at the red orchard tractor, eyes full of longing.
Qiao Bai has Aya first practice wrapping the graft union tight with ties.
In the noisy fruit market, Asui in a cream silk scarf looks up from behind apple baskets.

segments.action: In rainy season, Qiao Bai hangs damp ties to dry in the nursery shed.
Qiao Bai brushes resin from the grafting-knife sheath with a bristle brush.
At dawn, Qiao Bai checks bamboo-tag dates in the rootstock bed.
Qiao Bai hangs a raincoat on a shed post and listens to turtledoves.
In high summer, Qiao Bai shades the rootstock bed with sun netting.
Qiao Bai checks wax-seal softness so it will not turn brittle.
When autumn wind rises, Qiao Bai closes the scion cold-box lid by the berm.
On a blank phenology-book page Qiao Bai tries new stock-scion combo codes.
On a frost night, Qiao Bai lights a barn lantern and checks flashlight charge.
Qiao Bai wraps the scion bundles in a blanket against night freeze.
On a heavy-snow day, Qiao Bai sweeps thin snow from the old garden porch stone steps.
Qiao Bai warms hands with breath and tightens a tie.
In early spring, Qiao Bai trims wild roses by the porch.
Qiao Bai re-traces writing on the five bamboo tags.
Qiao Bai posts a new grafting schedule on the shed wall.
Around the Dragon Boat Festival, Qiao Bai smokes the cold box with mugwort against insects.
Qiao Bai rewets the scion hemp cloth.
Qiao Bai alone paces the rootstock bed, silently recalling the bud-graft mnemonic.
After rain, Qiao Bai pushes open the shed door and listens to eave water drip into the jar.
Qiao Bai swaps worn gloves for new ones.
Another dusk, Qiao Bai sits by the grafting knife listening to insects.
At night Qiao Bai rises and patches mud on the berm.
Qiao Bai stores newly arrived ties by color.
Qiao Bai wipes the Bai Garden plaque on the porch.
Qiao Bai checks orchard-tractor oil level.
Against a drawing Qiao Bai marks dense planting row spacing.
Qiao Bai wrings a mud-stained rag dry and hangs it.
On a full-moon night, Qiao Bai looks from the bed at seedlings; dew beads silver.
Qiao Bai tidies the berm so bamboo tags all face the same way.
Inside the cover Qiao Bai writes the new season's budbreak notes.
Qiao Bai polishes the two wind chimes.
Hearing market cart-and-horse sounds, Qiao Bai keeps cutting scions.
Qiao Bai glues a cracked bamboo basket.
In a shed corner Qiao Bai stacks rootstock seedlings ready for use.
Qiao Bai seals the cold box tight against night temperature swings.
Another Qingming, Qiao Bai sets a bunch of wildflowers on the porch.
Qiao Bai rolls drawings into a tube and binds them with a rubber band.
Qiao Bai tries a light wind-chime ring; the tone is crisp.
Qiao Bai sits silent in the shed, listening long to water dripping from leaf tips.
Qiao Bai cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Qiao Bai clears cut waste twigs from the bed ditch.
At dawn, Qiao Bai patrols the rootstock bed; the orchard tractor waits at the head.
Qiao Bai crouches to check mud depth on the tractor tires.
Qiao Bai walks to the shed shade; those earlier three Fuji scion bundles still wrap in wet hemp cloth.
A green spray cart rolls along the berm—long thin body, not the Bai Garden tractor.
Standing in the rootstock bed, Qiao Bai rechecks by bamboo-tag numbers whether unions are pushing new buds.
Qiao Bai hangs a wet raincoat on the berm wood rack.
Qiao Bai brushes mud flecks from the sleeve and glances back at the shed lamp.
After Grain Rain, Qiao Bai teaches a new apprentice to read bud-eye orientation in the rootstock bed.
Qiao Bai refolds sun-dried raincoats into the tractor toolbox.
In summer heat, Qiao Bai lays a wet cloth on the scion hemp wrap to keep moisture.
Qiao Bai checks the tractor rear bed and moves damp seedling bags to the upper tier.
On an autumn night, under a barn lantern, Qiao Bai rethreads mud-stained phenology loose pages.
Qiao Bai rotates updates among the five bamboo tags.
At first snow, Qiao Bai sweeps a narrow path across the porch threshold.
Qiao Bai reoils the practice folding knife and boxes it.
Hearing wind chimes ring lightly, Qiao Bai keeps revising the schedule.
Qiao Bai pushes open the shed door so a draft can carry damp away.
Qiao Bai hangs rain canvas on the porch.
Qiao Bai stores chipped old blades in an iron box.
At night Qiao Bai dreams of a survival-rate crash and, waking, writes bed numbers on a small blackboard.
Qiao Bai rinses bamboo tags with clear water.
Qiao Bai wipes the grafting schedule clean and reposts it.
Qiao Bai pulls weeds from berm stone seams.
Qiao Bai resticks bamboo tags in the berm; writing has faded some.
Before putting out the lamp, Qiao Bai glances once more at the grafting-knife edge.
Qiao Bai folds an indigo headscarf an apprentice left in the shed.
Hearing the market's closing horn, Qiao Bai rises and locks up.
By the charcoal fire Qiao Bai dries gloves.
Qiao Bai moves the wind chimes aside to show the just-repaired eaves.
Qiao Bai air-dries humidity test strips.
On the last phenology-book page Qiao Bai draws a survival-rate comparison.
Silently recalling tomorrow's bed numbers to graft, Qiao Bai steps out of the porch.
Qiao Bai drives the tractor to the wall foot, clearing scion-cutting floor space.
Hearing distant cockcrow, Qiao Bai blows out the barn lantern.
Another rainy night, Qiao Bai alone keeps watch over the scions until dawn.
Qiao Bai cuts newly arrived wax-seal blocks into small cubes.
Qiao Bai writes guest-ordered varieties on the small blackboard.
A storm breaks; the slope turns to mud; wind howls like a nursery alarm.
Lightning lights the shed; the tool bench rocks hard.
A crisp crack—the grafting knife blade chips; the cut edge goes rough.

segments.action: At the bed head comes nursery merchant Lao Tian with a bamboo basket of rootstock seedlings, build like Qiao Bai's but no straw hat.
The agronomy supervisor also arrives, white-coat badge damp with dew, talking beside Qiao Bai.
The supervisor points at the green spray cart's long thin tank, asking whether it belongs with the Bai Garden tractor.
The supervisor leaves; Qiao Bai alone remains in the rootstock bed.
Lao Tian unloads a bundle of rootstock seedlings, bows, and departs.
To the market comes girl Xiaoli in a light-brown headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Aya.
Xiaoli practices stacking apple baskets by fruit diameter; Qiao Bai shakes his head—her light-brown scarf is not Aya's indigo headscarf.
Xiaoli shyly bows her head and tightens the scarf.
Years later at dusk, Qiao Bai with a bandaged knee leans on a cane at the old garden porch.
